root_cause.text: The mctp-i2c slave event handler failed to initialize the output buffer value for I2C read requests, causing stack-uninitialized data from the i2c bus driver to be returned to readers instead of a proper default value.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds initialization of `*val = 0xff;` in the `I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED` and `I2C_SLAVE_READ_PROCESSED` cases of the `mctp_i2c_slave_cb()` function. The CVE description explicitly states that without this initialization, reads would return uninitialized stack memory ("val" from the i2c bus driver), which is a stack information disclosure vulnerability. The fix ensures all I2C read operations return a predictable 0xff value rather than leaking kernel stack contents.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix I2C slave read handling by adding READ_PROCESSED event case and returning a dummy value (0xff) for unsupported read operations.
intent_record.what: Added handling for I2C_SLAVE_READ_PROCESSED event case that falls through to I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED case, added a comment explaining MCTP I2C transport only uses writes, and added assignment of *val = 0xff before the break statement.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that when the I2C slave receives a READ_PROCESSED event, it resets the receive position counter and sets the response value to 0xff (all bits set). This prevents undefined behavior when the I2C master attempts to read from the slave, since MCTP I2C only uses writes for actual data transfer and reads should return a dummy value.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit ae4744e173fadd092c43eda4ca92dcb74645225a
Author: Jian Zhang <zhangjian.3032@bytedance.com>
Date:   Thu Jan 8 18:18:29 2026 +0800

    net: mctp-i2c: fix duplicate reception of old data
    
    The MCTP I2C slave callback did not handle I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED
    events. As a result, i2c read event will trigger repeated reception of
    old data, reset rx_pos when a read request is received.
    
    Signed-off-by: Jian Zhang <zhangjian.3032@bytedance.com>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The vulnerability root cause was that the mctp-i2c slave event handler failed to initialize the output buffer value for I2C read requests. The commit adds two key fixes: (1) A new case handler for I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED event that resets midev->rx_pos = 0 (lines 245-247), and (2) A check in mctp_i2c_recv() that returns early if rx_pos == 0 (lines 285-286), preventing stale data from being returned. These changes directly address the root cause by ensuring the buffer position is reset when a read request is received and preventing old data from being transmitted. The vulnerable construct (missing I2C_SLAVE_READ_REQUESTED handler) is now PRESENT with correct handling, making this a bug-fixing commit, not a bug-introducing one.
